question: (1+sqrt{5})² + (1-sqrt{5})² - 6 = ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the algebraic identity: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

Here, a = 1 and b = √5

⇒ 2(1² + (√5)²) − 6

⇒ 2(1 + 5) − 6 = 12 − 6 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: (1 + √5)² + (1 − √5)² − 6

Formula used: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

⇒ [(1)² + (√5)² + 2(1)(√5)] + [(1)² + (√5)² − 2(1)(√5)] − 6

⇒ [1 + 5 + 2√5] + [1 + 5 − 2√5] − 6

⇒ 6 + 2√5 + 6 − 2√5 − 6

⇒ (6 + 6 − 6) + (2√5 − 2√5)

⇒ 6 + 0

⇒ 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum and Difference of Squares

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) and (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Squaring of Surds

The square of a square root of a number is the number itself: (√x)² = x.

BODMAS Rule

Always solve exponents first, then perform addition and subtraction from left to right.
